title: Population History from Many Genomes
eyebrow: Lesson 5 · what changes when you have a whole sample
intro: Lesson 4 read history from one genome. This lesson asks what a sample of many genomes adds: genealogies for the whole sample, recent history from shared segments, selection, and the separate records of the Y chromosome and mitochondrial DNA. It also asks what SNP arrays can and cannot support, because many cohorts have arrays and not sequence.

Most methods here were built for human data, and the examples come from there. The last section reports what failed on a real array-based cohort from Asia: which outputs could not support a claim, how we found out, and what data would change that.
